function.name: ndim_engine_status
function.description:
Check the NDIM engine is reachable and see its resource limits and capabilities.

        Call first. Reports worker_limit (how many experiments can run at once; the engine queue holds 8) and
        what the engine cannot do ("unavailable").

function.name: ndim_list_workspaces
function.description: List research workspaces (id, name, domain, countries). Runs belong to exactly one workspace.

function.name: ndim_list_lessons
function.description:
Return the engine's teaching lessons (tutorials) and its synthetic sample field notes.

        Each lesson teaches one workflow (evidence, scenario, sensitivity). To run one here, plan it with its lesson_id,
        its question and the synthetic sample (consent="synthetic"); the researcher answers its check in the web app.
        The sample is synthetic, not real data.

function.name: ndim_plan_experiment
function.description:
Create a reviewable experiment plan. Nothing executes until ndim_start_experiment.

        Set skill explicitly: a question about how something might change adoption is a scenario, not evidence.
        Returns the steps, warnings and any blockers. Present them to the researcher before asking for approval,
        and for a scenario say plainly that their intervention is represented only by intervention_strength.

question.description: The researcher's question copied verbatim from their message. Do not rephrase, narrow, broaden or swap terms (e.g. do not turn "clean cooking" into "gas stoves" or "CHWs" into "health workers"), and do not add a prefix or context such as "in Rwanda" (the country has its own field). If it is too long or unclear, ask the researcher rather than rewriting it.
question.title: Question

evidence.description: Source narrative or field notes, in English. Non-English text is blocked by the engine. If you translate, tell the researcher and get their confirmation first.
evidence.title: Evidence

skill.description: Workflow. Choose it yourself; do not leave it to "auto", which guesses from keywords and falls back to evidence. "scenario": the question asks how an action, programme or condition might change, affect, increase, reduce, improve or influence adoption, trust or uptake ("How might training more CHWs change adoption?", "Would a subsidy help?", "What if we ran a radio campaign?"). It runs the evidence steps too and adds a baseline vs intervention comparison. This is the default for any question about change. "sensitivity": "how much", "how strong", "at what level", "is more effort worth it". "evidence": only what the notes contain (signals, themes, risks, trust) with no change in view.
skill.title: Skill

consent.description: "research_use" only if the researcher confirmed permission to use this evidence; "synthetic" for demo data; otherwise "unconfirmed". Never upgrade this yourself.
consent.title: Consent

model.description: Model family. agent_based ignores intervention strength, so it is blocked for scenario and sensitivity workflows.
model.title: Model

intervention_strength.description: The only intervention lever in the model. The researcher's intervention (e.g. "more trained CHWs") maps onto this abstract 0-1 value; the engine does not model CHW counts, prices or channels. 0.3 = moderate.
intervention_strength.title: Intervention Strength

expertise.description: Explanation level stored with the run.
expertise.title: Expertise

prior_run_ids.description: Completed runs that carry a researcher review, used as context only; they never change model parameters.
prior_run_ids.title: Prior Run Ids

strength_reason.description: Optional: why this intervention_strength. Quote the researcher only if they actually gave a value or level; never attribute the default to them. Shown to the researcher before approval and kept in the audit log.
strength_reason.title: Strength Reason

lesson_id.description: Only when running a tutorial from ndim_list_lessons: its id. skill must match the lesson, and the run then counts as that lesson in the web app, where the researcher answers its check.
lesson_id.title: Lesson Id

function.name: ndim_start_experiment
function.description:
Run an approved plan. Requires the researcher's explicit approval of this exact plan.

        Retries automatically while the engine queue is full. If it has not finished within wait_seconds,
        call ndim_wait_for_run.

approval_statement.description: The researcher's own words approving THIS plan, quoted from the conversation. Only call this tool after the researcher has actually approved; never write this text yourself. It is stored in an audit log.
approval_statement.title: Approval Statement

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for completion before returning progress.
wait_seconds.title: Wait Seconds

function.name: ndim_resume_experiment
function.description:
Resume a failed, interrupted or cancelled run from its saved checkpoints. Also needs researcher approval.

        Fails with 409 if the scientific code or environment changed since planning; then create a new plan.

approval_statement.description: The researcher's own words approving THIS plan, quoted from the conversation. Only call this tool after the researcher has actually approved; never write this text yourself. It is stored in an audit log.
approval_statement.title: Approval Statement

function.name: ndim_cancel_experiment
function.description: Request cancellation. In-flight tools finish first; completed checkpoints are kept.

function.name: ndim_wait_for_run
function.description: Wait until the run finishes or the timeout passes, then return its summary.

function.name: ndim_get_run
function.description: Get a run's status, encoded signals, per-simulation statistics, comparison and numerical checks.

include_trajectories.description: Include every daily trajectory point. Large (about 90 rows per simulation step); leave false unless you must plot or re-analyse.
include_trajectories.title: Include Trajectories

function.name: ndim_list_runs
function.description:
List what has already been run in a workspace, newest first, each with its matching tutorial.

        Not a way to answer a question: plan a new experiment. Run ids are withheld on purpose.

function.name: ndim_get_brief
function.description:
Return the engine-generated research brief (Markdown) for a completed run planned in this conversation.

        For an earlier run the researcher did not plan here, offer the matching tutorial instead of this brief.

function.name: ndim_compare_runs
function.description:
Tabulate completed runs side by side and audit their comparability.

        Aggregation happens here, deterministically, so you do not need to copy numbers between calls. Read
        comparability.notes: the comparison is only controlled when a single factor varies on identical evidence.

reference_run_id.description: For a one-at-a-time sweep: the base run. Each other run may then differ from it in exactly one factor.
reference_run_id.title: Reference Run Id

function.name: ndim_plan_sweep
function.description:
Create a set of scenario plans that differ only in the parameters you list. Nothing executes yet.

        Every run uses the scenario workflow (baseline vs intervention) on identical evidence. The engine is
        deterministic, so a sweep varies parameters; repeating an identical run adds nothing.

question.description: The researcher's question copied verbatim from their message. Do not rephrase, narrow, broaden or swap terms (e.g. do not turn "clean cooking" into "gas stoves" or "CHWs" into "health workers"), and do not add a prefix or context such as "in Rwanda" (the country has its own field). If it is too long or unclear, ask the researcher rather than rewriting it.
question.title: Question

evidence.description: Sent unchanged with every plan, so all runs share one source hash. Do not paste it repeatedly yourself; call this tool once.
evidence.title: Evidence

vary.description: Factors to vary and their values, e.g. {"narrative_influence": [0.2, 0.4, 0.6]}. Allowed factors: narrative_influence, initial_adoption, intervention_strength (0-1) and horizon_days (7-365). At most 12 values per factor.
vary.title: Vary

mode.description: one_at_a_time: a base run plus each value of each factor alone (attributable). grid: every combination (interactions, but differences cannot be attributed to one factor). At most 24 runs.
mode.title: Mode

function.name: ndim_run_sweep
function.description:
Run an approved sweep with the engine's queue limits respected, then compare the results.

        Needs the researcher's approval of the whole design. One failed run does not discard the others; check
        errors and comparison.excluded.

approval_statement.description: The researcher's own words approving THIS plan, quoted from the conversation. Only call this tool after the researcher has actually approved; never write this text yourself. It is stored in an audit log.
approval_statement.title: Approval Statement

function.name: ndim_journey_guide
function.description:
Explain the 13-stage NDIM journey: what each stage does, what it needs, and which need the researcher.

        Use it to describe the journey before starting, or when the researcher asks what a stage is.

function.name: ndim_journey_list
function.description: List a workspace's journeys, newest first. Resume one only if the researcher says it is theirs.

function.name: ndim_journey_start
function.description:
Start a 13-stage journey for the researcher's question. Nothing is scored or modelled yet.

        Call ndim_journey_guide first. Before this call, show the researcher the question in quotes exactly as you will
        pass it and wait for them to confirm or correct it.

question.description: The researcher's question copied verbatim from their message. Do not rephrase, narrow, broaden or swap terms (e.g. do not turn "clean cooking" into "gas stoves" or "CHWs" into "health workers"), and do not add a prefix or context such as "in Rwanda" (the country has its own field). If it is too long or unclear, ask the researcher rather than rewriting it.
question.title: Question

question_confirmation.description: The researcher's reply after you showed them the question in quotes, exactly as you will pass it, and asked them to confirm or correct it, e.g. "Yes, that is my question." Only call after they replied; never write this text yourself. If they corrected it, pass their corrected wording as question. It is stored in an audit log.
question_confirmation.title: Question Confirmation

function.name: ndim_journey_status
function.description: Where a journey stands: each stage's status, the records and their gate results, and the next stage.

function.name: ndim_journey_add_evidence
function.description:
Stages 1-2: add the researcher's records and run the SDMX gate on each (metadata, English, personal data,
        instruction-like text, duplicates). Records are stored unchanged; one record per story or note.

text.description: The story or field note, unchanged. English only: the encoder reads English keywords. If you translate, say so and get the researcher's confirmation.
text.title: Text

admin_unit.description: Place, as the researcher gave it, e.g. "Kicukiro / Niboye".
admin_unit.title: Admin Unit

source_name.description: Who or what the record came from, e.g. "Field team interview 4".
source_name.title: Source Name

period.description: When it was collected, e.g. "2026-Q2". Ask; do not guess.
period.title: Period

consent.description: "research_use" only if the researcher confirmed permission; "synthetic" for demo data; otherwise "unconfirmed".
consent.title: Consent

function.name: ndim_journey_record_decisions
function.description: Stage 3: record the researcher's accept or reject decision for each record. Only accepted records reach a model.

reason.description: The researcher's reason, if they gave one.
reason.title: Reason

approval_statement.description: The researcher's message giving these accept/reject decisions. Never decide for them. Copy it character for character from the researcher's message, however short ("Yes, continue." is fine). Never compose or expand it: a live agent recorded "Please proceed with drafting the policy output." when the researcher had written only "Yes, continue."
approval_statement.title: Approval Statement

function.name: ndim_journey_run_stage
function.description:
Run one journey stage (4-13) after the researcher agreed to continue. Stages must go in order.

        Order: encoding, compartmental, agents, digital (researcher's field observations), bayes, rl, regional
        (optional), graph, inoculation, policy (researcher approves the export). Re-running a stage clears the later
        stages that read it.

approval_statement.description: Required for digital and policy: the researcher's message giving their field observations (digital) or answering yes to the export question (policy). Copy it character for character from the researcher's message, however short ("Yes, continue." is fine). Never compose or expand it: a live agent recorded "Please proceed with drafting the policy output." when the researcher had written only "Yes, continue."
approval_statement.title: Approval Statement

observed_adoption.description: digital: adoption share the researcher observed in the field (0-1). Ask for it; there is no default.
observed_adoption.title: Observed Adoption

trust_shift.description: digital: change in trust the researcher observed since the evidence was collected, -1 to 1; 0 if they saw none. Ask.
trust_shift.title: Trust Shift

barrier_shift.description: digital: change in adoption barriers observed, -1 to 1; 0 if none. Ask.
barrier_shift.title: Barrier Shift

observed_series.description: digital, optional: observed adoption shares over time (at least 3), from the researcher's data. Lets the Bayesian stage fit the adoption curve; never fill it from model output.
observed_series.title: Observed Series

feedback_note.description: digital: where the observations come from.
feedback_note.title: Feedback Note

horizon_days.description: Days simulated by compartmental, agents, digital.
horizon_days.title: Horizon Days

priors.description: bayes, optional: trust_a, trust_b, barrier_a, barrier_b (Beta priors; defaults 6, 4, 4, 6).
priors.title: Priors

apply_to_twin.description: inoculation: also re-run the digital twin with the estimated message strength. Only if the researcher asks for it.
apply_to_twin.title: Apply To Twin

stages.title: Narrative intake
stages.does: Collects the stories or field notes, each with its place, source, period, language and consent.
stages.limits: Records are stored as given; nothing has been scored yet.

stages.title: SDMX gate
stages.does: Checks each record against the input contract: required metadata, English text, personal-data and prompt-injection patterns, duplicates. Runs automatically on intake.
stages.limits: The gate checks metadata and patterns only. It does not judge whether a record is true or representative.

stages.title: Repository
stages.does: The researcher accepts or rejects each record. Only accepted records reach any model.
stages.limits: Only accepted records reach any model. Decisions are frozen once encoding runs.

stages.title: Encoding
stages.does: Scores each accepted record for trust, adoption barrier, themes and misinformation risk with the English keyword encoder.
stages.limits: Scores come from English keywords in each record: interpretations for review, not measurements of trust or barriers in a community.

stages.title: Compartmental model
stages.does: Population-level adoption over time (S, M, T, I, R compartments) from the encoded signals.
stages.limits: Illustrative, uncalibrated curve driven by the keyword scores. Not a forecast.

stages.title: Agent-based model
stages.does: Household-level proxy with peer and media effects, as a second view of the same signals.
stages.limits: A deterministic proxy for household behaviour, not a simulation of real households. Not a forecast.

stages.title: Digital twin
stages.does: Feeds the researcher's field observations (observed adoption, trust and barrier shifts) back into a hybrid re-run. Needs real observations; there are no defaults.
stages.limits: Re-runs the hybrid model from the researcher's field observations. It is still uncalibrated: one observed level does not fit the model to reality.

stages.title: Bayesian update
stages.does: Updates the trust and barrier priors with the encoded signals; with an observed adoption series it also fits the adoption curve to those observations.
stages.limits: The signal update treats keyword scores as pseudo-observations; the number of pseudo-trials is a tool convention. An adoption curve is fitted only to an observed series the researcher supplied.

stages.title: RL optimizer
stages.does: Ranks four candidate actions by the tool's fixed assumed effects under the updated signals. The effects are assumptions set in the tool, not estimates.
stages.limits: The ranking restates the tool's fixed assumed lifts and costs; no data estimated them. It is not advice on which action to take.

stages.title: Regional analysis
stages.does: Groups the encoded evidence by place, or pools it. Optional.
stages.limits: Averages of keyword scores per place. A place with one or two records says little about the place. The rule of thumb is a threshold rule, not a model result.

stages.title: Knowledge graph
stages.does: Connects places, themes and trust/barrier signals as nodes and edges.
stages.limits: Links show that a place, a theme and a signal occur together in the records. They are not causal.

stages.title: Inoculation lab
stages.does: Drafts pre-bunking, refutation and short counter-messages from the diagnosis, and shows the tool's illustrative before/during/after adoption curves. Drafts need human review before any use.
stages.limits: Message drafts need human review before any use with people. The before/during/after curves use a fixed lift formula; they do not model message effects.

stages.title: Policy output
stages.does: Assembles the evidence grade, policy readiness, model summary and the audit trail into a draft for human review.
stages.limits: A draft for the research team's review: options for discussion, not recommendations. The evidence grade and readiness come from the number of records and encoder confidence only.

principles: Only records the researcher accepted reach a model.
Field feedback, evidence decisions and the export need the researcher's own words.
All scores are keyword heuristics and all curves are illustrative and uncalibrated.
guide.intro:
**The journey, in six phases**

1. Evidence: your field notes are stored as given, checked for metadata and personal data, and you accept or reject each one.
2. Encode: an English keyword heuristic scores trust, barriers and themes.
3. Model: illustrative, uncalibrated adoption curves from those scores.
4. Twin: the model re-run from your own field observations, then a signal update and a ranking of actions under the tool's fixed assumptions.
5. Strategy: place summaries, a map of which themes occur together, and message drafts for your review.
6. Export: a policy draft of options for your team to discuss, not recommendations.

**You decide at three points**

- Accepting or rejecting each record (stage 3)
- Giving your own field observations for the digital twin (stage 7)
- Approving the policy export (stage 13)
guide.next: Show the researcher the intro field word for word, as markdown. Then show their question back in quotes, exactly as you will pass it to ndim_journey_start (ask for it if they have not given one), and ask them to confirm or correct it. Call ndim_journey_start only after they reply, with that reply as question_confirmation. Guide the researcher one stage at a time. After each stage, explain in plain words what it did, the key numbers and their limits, then name the next stage and what it does, and ask whether to continue. Do not run the next stage until they say so. Stages marked researcher_decision need the researcher's own words (approval_statement) and, for the digital twin, their own field observations: ask for them, never invent or default them.

drafts.title: Before the rumour spreads in Gatenga
drafts.text: Some people may hear that clean cooking is only for wealthy households. Cost concerns are real, but they should be compared with fuel savings, time savings, financing options, and maintenance access. health worker can show the practical evidence in context.

drafts.title: Refutational preemption
drafts.text: Cost concerns are real, but they should be compared with fuel savings, time savings, financing options, and maintenance access. The correction should be specific, respectful, and paired with a practical next step rather than a generic denial.

drafts.title: Short social counter-message
drafts.text: Before deciding from a claim alone, ask health worker to compare the rumour with local demonstration evidence, household costs, safety practice, and repair support. Repeat the correction through health worker, a peer demonstration, and a follow-up household check after first use.
